rig: 2 × MI50 16 GiB on PCIe 3.0 x16 (peer-access full)
active_optimizations: TP-perf-c3: Q4_0 K+V fusion + F16-dst (full-attn layers)
TP-perf-c5: Q4_0 t128 schedule (default ON for fused gate+up)

models.dominant_lever: Q4_1 t128 already optimal for this dtype. Next 11% lever: ssm_out Q5_K (3120 calls × 54 µs). Next 10%: gdn_state_step (one per GDN layer per rank). Both are per-call-fixed operations — fusion of state_step with neighboring ops is the structural option.

ssm_out Q5_K (20% wall) is the biggest single-kernel lever. 113 µs/call for 6240 calls. A Q5_K t128 variant (mirror cycle 5 for Q5_K) could capture similar latency-hiding wins — estimated +5-10%. Secondary: 11440 unfused mmvq_q4_0 calls (attn_q + attn_output in full-attn layers) — write a 3-way Q+K+V or fold attn_output into a separate fusion.

Q4_1 has NO fused gate+up — 45760 individual mmvq_q4_1_t128 calls (50% of wall). Mirror cycles 1+3+5 for Q4_1: write mmvq_q4_1_gate_up_t128_dp4a + mmvq_q4_1_kv_f16dst_t128_dp4a. Estimated +5-10% (fewer launches + shared activation reads on the SAME shapes Q4_0 saved on).

BOTH Q8_0 kernels are 256t/block. The cycle-5 logic applies: write mmvq_q8_0_t128 + mmvq_q8_0_gate_up_t128 (mirror of cycle 5). Q8_0 is HBM-heaviest (largest weights, 29 GiB total) but the kernel is still latency-bound at batch=1. Estimated +4-8%.
Same shape as Qwen3.5-27B-Q4_0. Q5_K ssm_out → t128 variant is the +20% lever; remaining unfused Q4_0 calls (attn_q, attn_output) are the +13% lever.
Same as Qwen3.5-27B-Q8_0. Q8_0 t128 variants would lift both fused (+1685 ms) and unfused (+1370 ms) — combined ~89% of wall is on 256t Q8_0 kernels.

GDN state step is the biggest single kernel (19%). 50 µs/call × 3900 calls = 195 ms. The kernel has 2× the per-CU per-step work (head_dim=128, S_v=128). t128/half-warp variants likely won't help (it's already compute-bound, not launch-bound). Best lever: fold ssm_alpha+ssm_beta+ssm_dt+ssm_a into the state_step entry. Secondary: indexed_moe_mmvq_q4_k_* — already candle-port'd r4/r2 patterns; could add Q4_K t128 variants. NOTE: parity drift on this model (warm_argmax=1510 vs ref 11) is an open Bug 5 separate from perf — fix that before committing further perf work to qwen35moe.

cross_model_observations: Q4_0 27B / Q4_1 27B / Q8_0 27B all share the SAME non-MMVQ kernels (rmsnorm_q8_1_fused 7%, p2p_AR_RMSNorm 5%, attn_decode 3%, copyBuffer 1.5-2%). MMVQ dominates differently per dtype; cycles 1-5 only addressed Q4_0 fully. Q4_1 and Q8_0 still on 256t kernels.
ssm_out Q5_K is a consistent 20% lever on every qwen35 hybrid 27B model. Single-kernel optimization (Q5_K t128) would lift all four 27B configurations.

MoE A3B has a fundamentally different shape: GDN state_step is the biggest (19%) because A3B has many GDN layers (~32 of 40) and the state-step kernel is per-layer-per-token. Q8_0 is 28% (split across two kernels) because ssm_alpha/beta/etc are F32→Q8_0 converted at load.

rmsnorm_q8_1_fused holds steady at 6-7% across all 27B-class models. Per-call 28-30 µs × 8385 calls. Folding the input rmsnorm into the post-FFN AR (cycle-2-style but smarter) is the only meaningful structural option.

9B/Q4_1 has a different mix: per-layer overhead ratio is higher (32 layers vs 64) so per-call kernels (rmsnorm, AR, attention) take a relatively bigger share. Smaller models gain less from MMVQ optimization.
out_of_scope_for_perf_until_correctness: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (qwen35moe) — parity drift warm_argmax=1510 vs ref 11. Fix Bug 5 first; perf optimisations on broken output don't count.
